text_blocks.snippet: Generally, insurance does not cover ozone therapy as it's considered an alternative or complementary therapy, and not part of conventional medicine. Insurance companies typically only cover treatments that are scientifically proven and widely accepted by the medical community.

list.title: Alternative Therapy:
list.snippet: Ozone therapy is often categorized as an alternative or complementary therapy, meaning it's not typically part of standard medical practice.

list.title: Lack of Scientific Evidence:
list.snippet: Many insurance companies require evidence-based research to support the efficacy and safety of a treatment before they will cover it. Ozone therapy is still undergoing research and its effectiveness is not yet fully established.

list.title: FDA Approval:
list.snippet: The FDA does not recognize ozone therapy as a proven treatment for any condition.

list.title: Cost Considerations:
list.snippet: Since insurance typically doesn't cover it, patients are often responsible for the full cost of ozone therapy treatments, according to multiple sources.

list.title: Individual Plans:
list.snippet: While rare, some insurance plans may offer limited coverage for specific ozone therapy applications or if it's used in conjunction with other covered treatments. It's always best to check with your specific insurance provider for accurate coverage information.

list.title: Alternative Payment Options:
list.snippet: Some clinics offer flexible spending accounts (FSAs) or health savings accounts (HSAs), or may have their own self-pay plans, to help offset the cost for patients, according to a holistic wellness center.
